I don't know where to ask this question so I'll just ask here. What makes a good villain, whether movies or comics? What makes them so special? I've seen a lot of "X did nothing wrong" and even participated in some of that thought (basic bitch example: the Galactic Empire was better than the Rebel scum) but I still don't fully understand why villains are at times more what we want heroes to be than the actual heroes.

1) They have some justification for what they do and it's not irrational and pointless.

2) They mostly win their battles until the very end.

3) They have a cool costume or outfit.
You don't know he is the villain until too late.

IMO: The best, and most disturbing villans are the ones that make us recognize the villain in ourselves. The type of character that takes rational views to a logical extreme, and throughout a story slowly make you question who the villain really is. The main character in the movie "Law Abiding Citizen" is a great example of bluring the lines beyween antagonist and protagonist.
